summary: Search-target (TreeStrap) experiment on the n-tuple leaf: a training-time fair expectimax that mirrors the engine's search bit for bit and returns score-only backups for every internal node (search_train.rs), the trainer's search actor with visited-state and tree targets and a warm-start validation point, a CHECK gate comparing the training search against the engine's column values and decisions; the theory, the preregistered experiment with three fresh leases and the stage driver; ran the gates, the smoke run, the two warm-started search-actor arms, the freeze and the one-shot 512-game screen; wrote the analysis, the result record, the approach page section, the web figures and the log entry.
validationPerformed: cargo test --release (15 unit tests, including the training search matching the engine's column values bit for bit and collecting internal nodes)
gate binary on the frozen tables (gate --weights): all CHECK gates including train-search-vs-engine (gates.log), and gate --weights on each of the two new table files before the screen lease opened
analyze.py evaluated the preregistered gate and the readings beside it from the screen artifact; compare.py reports written for eighteen contrasts
npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint, check-mdx, check-figures and check-tokens under web/
every compact artifact of the run and the two screened table files (zstd) were published to the public research archive and verified (runs/RUN-20260907T012358Z-a00ecdf0/published.jsonl)
limitations: Self-reported contribution; not yet independently reviewed.

The owner asked for the leaf to be trained on the boards the search evaluates rather than only the one-ply visited ones, and for advice on whether the depth-aware n-tuple direction has run its course; the model designed the training-time search, the score-only backup semantics, the two arms, the gate and the protocol, and ran everything on the same workstation as the four earlier n-tuple experiments.
